what_it_does: Running a large AI model on a phone or laptop requires storing billions of numbers (the model's learned weights) somewhere; flash storage (the same kind of chip inside a USB drive or SSD) has enough capacity but is too slow to feed a processor quickly, because data must travel from the flash chip through a narrow interface cable (PCIe) to reach the CPU. AiF sidesteps that bottleneck by placing small multiply-and-add circuits directly inside the flash chip, so the math happens where the data already lives, exploiting the chip's own wide internal data paths that are far faster than the external cable. The paper also introduces two new ways to read flash cells tuned to how AI weight data is organized, and a streamlined error-correction scheme that quadruples effective internal read speed.
